meta.description: Analyze single-cell ATAC-seq with Signac/ArchR (R) and SnapATAC2 (Python alternative). Use when processing scATAC fragments, choosing a framework, calling consensus peaks, running TF-IDF/LSI while diagnosing the depth component, scoring chromVAR motif deviations against GC-matched backgrounds, detecting homotypic vs heterotypic doublets, or deciding whether to binarize the count matrix.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs/results across any of the 7 outputs; all reported statistics (ARI, DA p-values, chromVAR z-scores, doublet recall) came from real computation on data explicitly labeled synthetic.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic/prescriptive medical conclusions in any output; the skill is a research-tooling method doc with no patient-facing claims.

methodological_ground.detail: No fallacies observed; the skill actively guards against double-dipping (DA on a same-clustering peak set), circular peak calling, motif!=TF overclaiming, and gene-activity-as-RNA overclaiming, and held up under adversarial (Input 7) and scope-boundary (Input 6) probing.

code_usability.detail: Close call, documented in detail: the skill's documented `RunChromVAR()` call (Input 5) throws on the installed Signac 1.17.1 -- confirmed via Signac's own NEWS.md as an intentional removal, not an environment fluke. Scored PASS rather than FAIL because (a) it is one broken wrapper inside an otherwise-verified multi-step, multi-route skill, not systemic breakage; (b) the underlying computation is trivially recoverable via the same package's still-exported lower-level API, which this audit used successfully; and (c) SKILL.md's Version Compatibility section gives explicit, working generic guidance for exactly this class of API-drift failure ('introspect the installed package and adapt... rather than retrying'), which is what enabled recovery. This is captured as a P1 recommendation and the dynamic-score floor already forces a one-tier grade downgrade.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of every promised use case (QC, LSI/depth diagnosis, clustering, peak calling, DA, chromVAR, gene activity, doublets, 3-framework decision table); correctness docked for two execution-verified currency defects (RunChromVAR removed entirely from current Signac; NucleosomeSignal/TSSEnrichment/StringToGRanges deprecated).

reliability.note: Common Errors table covers 10 real failure modes with symptom/cause/fix; Version Compatibility section gives generic, empirically-verified recovery guidance for API drift, which is what let this audit recover from the RunChromVAR break.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is 208 lines; usage-guide and examples are cleanly separated; workflow is linear with no redundant round-trips.

agent_usability.note: Governing Principle up front gives the 'why' before the 'how'; extensive, specific error-prevention (10-row Common Errors table, repeated genome-build-mismatch warning); feedback design is mostly explicit but not always exact on expected print output.

human_usability.note: Quick Start prompts match natural researcher phrasing; Version Compatibility section is an above-average forgiveness mechanism for a static doc, but there is no explicit 'when not to use' section.

security.note: No credentials, no eval/exec of raw user strings, standard path-based file I/O only.

maintainability.note: Clean modular separation (SKILL.md / usage-guide / 2 example scripts); empirically confirmed deterministic outputs (TF-IDF/SVD/clustering bit-identical across two unseeded reruns) make the pipeline genuinely testable.

agent_specific.note: Precise, specific trigger description; SKILL.md well under the 500-line budget; 7-skill Related Skills list gives clean composability boundaries; idempotency confirmed for LSI/clustering but chromVAR's own determinism was not independently re-verified (P2); no dedicated escape-hatch section (P2).

key_strengths: Governing Principle up front gives agents the epistemic 'why' (near-binary sampling, disfavored binarization, circular peak-calling) before the 'how', producing correct pushback on both adversarial and scope-boundary test inputs (7/7 assertions passed across Inputs 6-7).

The core TF-IDF/LSI/depth-diagnosis/clustering pipeline is empirically validated end to end on synthetic ground-truth data: symptom-based (not positional) depth-component diagnosis, ARI=0.97 cluster recovery.
Differential accessibility testing (logistic regression with fragment depth as a latent variable) is statistically sound and recovered 85% of true differential peaks against synthetic ground truth.

Version Compatibility guidance ('introspect the installed package... adapt rather than retrying') gave a real, working recovery path when the documented RunChromVAR() call turned out to be removed from the current Signac release.
Extensive, specific Common Errors table (10 rows) and framework/matrix-type decision tables give strong error-prevention and reduce trigger ambiguity.

recommendations.title: RunChromVAR() removed from current Signac -- chromVAR section fails as documented
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's chromVAR code (obj <- RunChromVAR(obj, genome=...)) throws 'could not find function "RunChromVAR"' on Signac 1.17.1, the version the skill's own Version Compatibility note targets (1.13+).
recommendations.root_cause: Signac's own NEWS.md confirms RunChromVAR() and AddChromatinModule() were removed because the chromVAR package became unavailable in Bioconductor 3.23; SKILL.md was not updated to reflect this.
recommendations.fix: Replace the RunChromVAR() call with chromVAR's own addGCBias/matchMotifs/getBackgroundPeaks/computeDeviations sequence (verified working in this audit's run/03_chromvar_and_da.R), or explicitly call out the break and the version boundary in Version Compatibility.

recommendations.title: biovizBase is a required but undocumented dependency
recommendations.problem: GetGRangesFromEnsDb(), the documented way to build the Annotation() used throughout the workflow, throws 'Please install biovizBase' unless that package is already present.
recommendations.root_cause: usage-guide.md's Prerequisites section lists Signac, EnsDb, BSgenome, chromVAR, motifmatchr, JASPAR2020, TFBSTools, scDblFinder, ArchR, and snapatac2/scanpy, but omits biovizBase.
recommendations.fix: Add biovizBase to the Prerequisites install block in usage-guide.md.

recommendations.title: NucleosomeSignal(), TSSEnrichment(), and StringToGRanges() are deprecated in the installed Signac release
recommendations.problem: All three documented functions emit 'deprecated, use ATACqc()/etc.' warnings on Signac 1.17.1; they still work today but are on the same removal path RunChromVAR already took.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md and the example scripts were written against an earlier Signac API surface and have not been refreshed for the 1.17.x deprecation cycle.
recommendations.fix: Note the ATACqc() consolidation in Version Compatibility and update example code to current idioms before the next Signac release drops them.

recommendations.title: No explicit escape-hatch / out-of-scope section
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md has no dedicated 'when not to use this' section; scope boundaries are only implied through prose caveats and the Related Skills list.
recommendations.root_cause: The skill is written as a dense reference/method doc rather than an agent-facing decision procedure with explicit stop conditions.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'Escape Hatches' subsection pointing to single-cell/multimodal-integration when scRNA-equivalent single-cell resolution is requested, and to a human/statistician when a motif-to-TF causal claim is needed.

recommendations.title: chromVAR reproducibility across reruns not independently verified
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md never calls set.seed() anywhere; this audit confirmed the TF-IDF/SVD/clustering path is deterministic by virtue of Seurat/Signac internal defaults, but did not re-run the multi-minute chromVAR getBackgroundPeaks/computeDeviations step twice to confirm the same holds there.
recommendations.root_cause: chromVAR's background-peak sampling is not obviously internally seeded, and audit time budget did not allow a second full run.
recommendations.fix: A fix/re-audit pass should run computeDeviations() twice on identical input and diff the z-score matrix; add an explicit set.seed() call ahead of the chromVAR block if it varies.
